name: Silicom Ltd.
blurb: Silicom is an Israeli supplier of high-performance networking hardware - smart NICs (network interface cards), FPGA-based accelerators, edge appliances and switch fabric components - sold mostly to OEMs that bake the boards into their own cybersecurity, SD-WAN, telecom and cloud-edge products. It is a classic small-cap design-win business: revenue depends on how many customer programs ramp into volume each year. Lod-headquartered, founded 1987.
recent: Q1 2026 revenue of $19.1m was up 33% year-over-year and ahead of guidance; Q2 was guided to $20-21m and full-year 2026 to $82-83m. The balance sheet ended Q1 with no debt and about $109m of working capital and marketable securities ($63m cash and equivalents, $63m inventory). Management has banked four design wins in the first four months of 2026 against a target of seven to nine for the year, including a tier-one cybersecurity edge system worth over $1m of 2026 orders and an inference-specific NIC under co-development with one of two large AI compute customers, with hyperscaler proof-of-concept deployments slated for H2 2026.
